name: Wrapped-row splice parity

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: headed WASM WebGPU TextArea edit fixture
hypothesisMarkdown:
# Hypothesis

For a same-length, single-line edit that changes the wrapped visual-row count, the retained layout map updates only the edited row and shifts the following visual-row starts without rebuilding unaffected rows. Full layout remains the oracle for every buffer/display coordinate.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
# Measurement plan

Add a deterministic differential test with a shaper whose wrapping changes for a same-length replacement. Compare every byte boundary and all visual-row offsets with a full layout update, then run the focused headed WASM/WebGPU TextArea edit fixture and inspect its screenshot.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
# Expected outcome

The incremental map shapes one row, retains every other layout, preserves visual coordinate parity, and moves only following visual-start metadata when the changed row adds or removes wraps.
reportMarkdown:
## Wrapped-row splice parity

The differential map test now covers a same-byte-length edit that reduces the edited logical row from three wrapped visual rows to two. It compares every valid UTF-8 byte boundary with a full layout update, including the row after the changed row.

Focused headed WASM/WebGPU validation of `/performance/text-area-edit` passed at DPR 1 and DPR 2 with the edited character and caret rendered correctly. `check-source-guard` and `git diff --check` also passed.

Accept: the existing splice implementation already updates following `visual_start` metadata by the visual-row delta, and the new parity coverage proves the required coordinate behavior without expanding the fast-path eligibility.
decisionMarkdown:
## Decision

Accept the wrapped-row parity coverage. The splice implementation remains limited to same-length, single-line, unprojected, unstyled edits and falls back for all other edits.
